PART 1. Introduction
Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the Commission’s performance
management framework. The Commission’s strategic plan for 2025-2029 translates the
political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general
objectives. This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the
actions of all Commission services with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for 2025-
2029 (OIB Management Plan 2025). This outlook defines a set of multiannual objectives and
indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used for planning and
reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 management plan sets out what OIB intends to deliver this year to contribute to
these multiannual objectives (part 2). It also describes how OIB will contribute to the common
objective of building a modern and sustainable public administration (part 3). The main outputs
with their indicators and targets are presented in Annexes 1 and 2.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for OIB.

PART 2. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities in 2026
General Objective 8: A modern high-performing and sustainable European
Commission.
Specific Objective 8.1: The Commission’s office infrastructure and space are future-
proof and uphold to the highest environmental standards
Buildings and office infrastructure
Since 2021, the building strategy of the Commission aims for a reduction of 25% of its space
and 50% of its number of buildings in Brussels by 2030. In 2026, OIB will continue to work
towards reducing the Commission’s overall office space and the number of buildings in
Brussels accordingly. Two new energy-efficient buildings will be occupied by the Commission’s
services in Dynamic Collaborative space in 2026: T211 and MO34. The target remains a
reduction to 580 000 m² of office space by 2030.
For the EC Representations in the EU Member States, rental prolongations and new market
prospections in coordination with the EP are in preparation for Bucharest, Ljubljana, Madrid,
Riga and Tallin. A decision on the future premises of the Representation in Rome is expected.
Ongoing works in the premises of the Representation in Bratislava are expected to be finalised
by the end of 2026.
Decarbonisation
Under its longstanding commitment to improve its
environmental performance under EMAS (1), OIB
implements the objectives of the greening action
plan (2), supporting the Commission’s role as a
modern, green public administration. This includes
objectives to minimise the environmental impact
of Commission buildings and services in Brussels:
✓ Reduction of total final energy consumption of staff in Brussels by -40% by 2030 as
compared to 2019 (3).
✓ Reduction of at least 30 383 MWh of primary energy consumption by 2026 (-9%) as
compared to 2018-2019 values to respect the PLAGE (4) obligations.
✓ Reduction of the carbon life cycle impact of buildings (‘in use’ and ‘embodied’ CO) by

38% by 2030 as compared to 2019.

Furthermore, as the Greening Progress Review confirms that Real Estate is a key contributor to

domain.
Specific Objective 8.2: Provide and maintain a modern, safe and dynamic working
environment for colleagues
Development of new building projects
OIB will continue to secure and adapt premises for
staff by proactively prospecting new buildings suitable
for a modern administration following the governance
and administrative procedures in place. The sale of
Commission buildings in 2024 has led to an
invigoration of the prospection activity which will be
actively pursued in 2026 safeguarding the interests of
the Commission and optimising the realisation of the
OIB objectives. In addition, construction works will continue for the new conference centre. All
these projects incorporate the principles of the New European Bauhaus and support the
initiative of the Brussels-Capital Region to improve the European Quarter.
OIB also supports the renovation, adaptation and maintenance of the buildings of the EC
Representations in the EU Member States and the day-to-day facility management operations.
Dynamic Collaborative Space
The building strategy of the Commission targets the
smarter and greener usage of each m². OIB
implements this strategy by converting office space
into ‘Dynamic Collaborative Space’ (DCS), a modern
set up which contributes to enhance teamwork,
facilitate knowledge sharing and which can be adapted to evolving needs and priorities of staff
and services. In 2026, DCS will be rolled out in the following buildings:
✓ BERL (7) (partial)
✓ CHAR (8) (partial)

New collaborative spaces will be implemented in the EC Representations, taking into
consideration the specific requirements of the different premises in EU Member States.
Health & Safety
OIB continues to propose preventive measures to maintain and improve the health and safety
of staff at work. Training sessions and communication actions are addressed to staff on
awareness raising, prevention, protection, evacuation, ergonomics and equality/access. OIB
prevention advisors support Commission services on all relevant aspects in relation to works
and buildings. In particular, in the fields of prevention and protection, emergency preparedness
and response, accessibility and ergonomics, OIB:
✓ carries out annual evacuation exercises in all EC buildings in Brussels and supports DG HR
services in case of emergency situations.
✓ provides advice and trainings on relevant aspects of safety at work such as building safety,
accessibility and compliance, fire prevention, ergonomics, prevention of risks, etc.
✓ contributes to DG HR awareness raising campaigns related to occupational health and
safety for staff and services.
✓ carries out occupational risk assessments per post in EC premises in Brussels on a
continuous basis.
✓ participates in all CPPT (9) and OHS (10) meetings.
✓ will provide advice for the implementation of Health and Safety policies in the EC
Representations in the EU Member States.
OIB activities also contribute to the health and safety management system in Brussels.
Sustainable transport and mobility
OIB continues its efforts towards a 100% zero or low
emission fleet of service cars in 2027 with the aim
of having 98% zero or low emission vehicles (11) by the
end of 2026 out of which 80% fully electric. The
management of the fleet will be further digitalised by
integrating car data in the current EC-Transport
system, allowing for better follow up (of e.g. mileage
and technical alerts). In the EU Member States, OIB also supports the greening of the EC
Representations’ car fleet.
(9) Joint Committee for Prevention and Protection at Work
(10) Interinstitutional Occupational Health & Safety Network
(11) Excluding specific types of vehicles where low/zero emissions are unavailable in the market or
do not have the necessary autonomy to ensure long distance journeys

In the context of the new EC Green Commuting policy, OIB promotes sustainable staff mobility.
OIB supports the green commuting of staff by expanding bike areas in its buildings, installing
charging points for electric bikes and vehicles improving changing rooms and facilities.
In addition to modernising and increasing the green commuting infrastructure, OIB supports the
introduction of the new benefit scheme for cyclists and the lending of service bikes to help
staff test and start sustainable commuting. OIB also provides a sufficient capacity of service
bikes.
Modern office environment
OIB supports the optimisation of a dynamic working environment through a client-centric
approach that adapts to evolving needs and priorities of staff and services to ensure a fit-for-
purpose, future-proof workplace for staff. In 2026, OIB will:
✓ provide adapted furniture and equipment for the dynamic working environment and reduce
the use of office supplies.
✓ enhance digital visual design and printing activities to ensure efficiency, cost-effectiveness
and innovation.
✓ continue to provide cost-effective and clear signage in the EC buildings, in line with the EC
visual identity charter (12), to contribute to a modern and coherent corporate working
environment for EC staff.
✓ further roll-out the digitisation of incoming mail across the Commission.
✓ preserve, process and digitise the historical archives of the European Commission in view of
their public opening and long-term digital preservation.
Specific Objective 8.3: Provide agile and sustainable services for colleagues
Childcare services in Brussels
In Autumn 2025, OIB has 754 children enrolled in its nurseries and kindergartens (occupancy
rate of 82%). 2 736 children are enrolled in the after-school childcare for the school year
2025/2026 (occupancy rate of 103% (13)). 336 outdoor childcare places are available in the
European Interinstitutional Centre (CIE), with an additional reserve of 96 places in Brussels. The
main objectives for OIB are to:
✓ provide sufficient capacity for children in childcare services.
✓ implement the long-term strategy for childcare services.
✓ further integrate the green dimension in its childcare operations (14).

no negative impact on the delivered childcare services.

playground etc.)

Childcare services in Ispra
At the time of this report, the nursery for children between 6 months and 4 years has a
capacity of 88 places. The afterschool childcare service accommodates children between 4 and
11 years and has a capacity of 105 places. During school holidays and in the summer, specific
whole-day activities are organised. The main objectives for the childcare services in Ispra are
to:
✓ provide sufficient capacity for children.
✓ ensure the timely opening of the new ‘Icaro’ garderie (15).
✓ further integrate the green dimension in its childcare operations.
Restaurant and cafeteria services in Brussels
In 2026, OIB will continue to consolidate and
optimise the implementation of its catering
model and is planning to:
✓ reopen three to four cafeterias and two
restaurants.
✓ further reduce the catering environmental
footprint (by reducing disposable packaging, sorting organic waste, using recyclable
containers, assessing the potential implementation of the good food label (or equivalent),
etc.). This also involves training catering staff on HACCP (16) standards and environmental
legislation.
The catering model will be continuously analysed and adapted to take into account the
evolution of the Brussels catering market and the outcome of the Greening Progress Review.
Restaurant and cafeteria services in Ispra
In Ispra, OIB manages two restaurants, one ‘VIP’ restaurant, one cafeteria and one clubhouse
bar/restaurant. All banqueting activities for the site fall under the responsibility of OIB. The
main objectives are to:
✓ closely monitor the advancement of the refurbishment of the main restaurant facilities, led
by the Joint Research Centre (JRC).
✓ closely supervise the adequate implementation of the contract for the provision of
restaurant and bar services in the clubhouse restaurant.
✓ further integrate, where possible, sustainable and environmentally responsible practices in
catering operations.
Regarding the lodgings in Ispra, OIB will:

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable
levels through cost-effective controls.
OIB has established an internal control system tailored to its particular characteristics and
circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will be assessed on an
ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to an annual assessment covering all
internal control principles.
A. Human resource management
The human resource management of OIB remains fully aligned with the corporate HR strategy,
dedicated to an efficient and dynamic resource allocation as well as swift internal recruitment
processes while emphasising OIB’s five core values (kindness, teamwork, trust, recognition and
transparency). OIB is fully dedicated to foster equality in its staff policies in line with the
common Commission objectives. In 2026, the Office will:
✓ maintain an equitable percentage of women in management (56% in 2024) and deputy
positions as well as strive towards geographically balanced representation. It will also
continue its investment in inventive staff engagement initiatives for all colleagues (18).
✓ promote training courses, well-being activities and initiatives on individual and structural
level.
B. Digital transformation and data management
Digital transformation
OIB will continue the modernisation of its IT landscape in 2026, by implementing the following
actions under strategic objectives #3, #4 and #5 of the corporate digital strategy (19):
Objective #1 ‘Foster a digital culture’
✓ OIB will enhance its efforts in upskilling staff on data and IT literacy by making sure that all
staff understand and use Commission platforms and tools correctly and are acquainted
with the appropriate use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to accomplish their tasks.

(19) Please see Annex 2, Section B (Page 19) for further details
10

OIB will ensure that staff participates in adequate training sessions or workshops. AI
capabilities will be integrated in OIB information systems as needed and as requested by the
business.
Objective #3 ‘Empower business-driven digital transformation’
✓ The Archis (20) information system will make use of AI to improve optical character
recognition and keywords extraction from digitised historical archives documents.
✓ The EC Transport system will be further enhanced to improve dispatching and fleet
management capabilities, with a focus on car data and geolocation.
✓ The OIBScore solution will be further expanded to include Strategic Planning and
Programming indicators.
✓ The REMIS system will be extended to incorporate new capabilities for event space
reservation, building energy efficiency, and safety device location.
Objective #4 ‘Ensure a seamless digital landscape’
✓ In line with the Reuse-Buy-Build approach, OIL will start using the REMIS facilities
management functions, further strengthening synergies between the two Offices.
✓ Legacy IT systems will continue to be replaced by new IT systems developed with latest
cloud technologies, such as Memora (21).
✓ By the end of 2025, 50% of OIB systems will have been migrated to the cloud. In 2026 and
in line with DIGIT’s recommendations (22), the cloudification process will be expanded to
include three modules of the Archis information system: ArchisScanning,
ArchisScanningEXTRa and HistOrga.
Objective #5 ‘Sustain a green, resilient and secure infrastructure’
✓ To ensure a resilient and secure infrastructure, OIB, in full alignment with EC Cybersecurity
Strategy, will continue enhancing cybersecurity measures, involve senior management in
risk reviews, and promote frequent reporting on IT security matters. Additionally, OIB will
support sustainable IT practices through the EMAS initiative and ensure compliance with
corporate IT and information security rules.
Data management
OIB will continue implementing actions in all four key areas of the corporate data policies,
with the objective of improving its data maturity level to ‘Established’ by end of 2026. To
enhance data management, OIB will review and update all its data assets in the EC data
catalogue and continue to participate in the central data acquisition yearly exercises. To
reinforce ownership and responsibilities, the Office will review and update the data owners

and stewards for all its data assets. OIB will continue to apply the FAIR (Findable, Accessible,
Interoperable, Reusable) principles and adhere to corporate policies on reference data
management to ensure data quality. OIB will revise the metadata quality in the EC Data
Catalogue and contribute to the HR Family Data Catalogue. Finally, to further develop data
skills of staff, OIB will continue to promote corporate data training programmes and local
capacity-building initiatives, such as data protection trainings.
Data Protection
OIB ensures a rigorous follow-up and respects the data protection rules in place. The Data
Protection Coordinator provides required reports to the Head of Service and Data Protection
Officer of the Commission. In 2026, OIB will continue to monitor compliance with the data
protection regulation and the Data Protection Management System (DPMS) records will be
updated accordingly. OIB will also continue to organise mandatory training courses for
colleagues. By the end of 2026, 85% of colleagues will be trained on data protection
compliance.
C. Sound financial management
OIB's central financial unit will continue to fulfil its guiding role to ensure that OIB runs its
finances efficiently and maintains a low level of payment delays (23). The finance unit
will:
✓ monitor the budget programming and execution to ensure a flexible response to unforeseen
demands and an efficient use of resources. The finance unit will also ensure regular
management reporting.
✓ continue to optimise the procurement activities.
✓ continue to optimise and modernise the tools used and the internal operational procedures,
e.g. through regular follow-up and support.
The ex-post controls are part of the supervision activities to ensure that the Authorising
Officer by Delegation has reasonable assurance that resources have been used in accordance
with all relevant principles of legality and regularity. The materiality threshold for errors in
payments and at closure is established at max 2% of the allocated budget.
D. Fraud risk management
In 2025, OIB adopted a revised Anti-Fraud Strategy (AFS). The revised AFS and action plan
are aligned with the Commission Anti-Fraud Strategy and action plan and include corporate-
level actions linked to the following objectives:
✓ Foster digitalisation and use of IT tools to fight fraud.
(23) Please see Annex 2, Section C (Page 20) for further details
12

✓ Reinforce the Commission's anti-fraud governance and maintain a high level of
coordination and cooperation among departments and executive agencies.
✓ Contribute to strengthening the culture of ethics and anti-fraud in the Commission.
In 2026, the relevant actions in the OIB Anti-Fraud Action Plan (24) will be implemented.
E. Sound environmental management
OIB continues to reduce CO emissions from its staff missions to reach the targeted 50%
2
reduction versus 2019 (25). An awareness-raising session will be organised to present the main
changes to the guide to missions in 2026.
Local actions include the promotion of eco-friendly travel in the context of the annual mobility
week and safe cycling training sessions offered for commuters (26).
As OIB is moving buildings in early 2026, local participation in the BEST summer 2026, and
related, actions, in particular as a Hub building during that time, cannot yet be confirmed at the
time of writing of this report.
OIB continues to engage its EMAS (1) network and organise regular meetings. At the bi-annual
network meetings, each unit is represented by a dedicated ambassador. The network supports
staff ideas and initiatives to strengthen the sound environmental management in the Office.
OIB’s ‘Green Platform’ (27)) promotes awareness and knowledge about sound environmental
actions and campaigns.
Further promotion and information on environmental topics will be provided through corporate
communication channels (MyIntracomm, monthly Staff Matters Newsletter) and local
communication channels in OIB and other DGs/services (e.g. intranets, newsletters, collaborative
platforms and messages on physical monitors).
